learn.hook: An elephant, a goat, a cat and a mouse line up. Who is heaviest? Who is lightest?
points: We can order animals and objects from heaviest to lightest.
Lift two things, one in each hand, to feel which is heavier.
Bigger things are often heavier, but not always: a small stone can be heavier than a big balloon.
Half of 1 kg is 500 g. If a whole pumpkin weighs 1 kg, half of it weighs 500 g.

example.q: A pumpkin weighs 2 kg. Amma cuts it into two equal halves. How much does each half weigh?

learn.reallife: At the vegetable shop, a big cabbage may be lighter than a small bag of potatoes. Lift and feel!

games.title: Heavy or light?
items: A big balloon is always heavier than a small stone.
Size does not decide weight. The stone is heavier.
Lifting two things helps us compare their weights.
The heavier one feels harder to hold up.
A school bag full of books is lighter than an empty one.
Half of a 4 kg watermelon weighs 2 kg.

quiz.q: Which is the heaviest?
quiz.explain: A cow is much bigger and heavier than the others.
steps: Think about the real animals: a cow, a hen, a rabbit, a goat.
A cow is much bigger than all the others.
So the cow is the heaviest.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the real animals

quiz.q: Which is the lightest?
steps: A book, a shoe and a brick all have some weight you can feel.
So the feather is the lightest.

quiz.q: Half of 1 kg is how many grams?
quiz.mistake: Thinks half of 1 kg is 50 g

quiz.q: A whole pumpkin weighs 1 kg. Ravi buys half of it. How much does his piece weigh?
steps: The whole pumpkin is 1 kg = 1000 g.

quiz.q: Mini lifts a bag of cotton and a bag of salt of the same size. Which feels heavier?
quiz.explain: Salt is packed tightly and is much heavier than the same size bag of cotton.
steps: The bags are the same size.
Salt is packed tightly; cotton is fluffy and light.
So the bag of salt feels heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same size means the same weight

quiz.q: Put in order from heaviest to lightest: dog, ant, horse.
quiz.explain: A horse is heaviest, then a dog, then a tiny ant.
steps: Heaviest to lightest means biggest weight first.
A horse is heaviest, then a dog, and a tiny ant is lightest.

quiz.q: A melon weighs 3 kg. It is cut into 2 equal halves. How much does each half weigh?
Which is true?
options: A small iron ball can be heavier than a big beach ball
quiz.explain: Weight depends on what a thing is made of, not just its size.
steps: Weight depends on what a thing is made of, not only its size.
A small iron ball is solid metal; a big beach ball is mostly air.
So a small iron ball can be heavier than a big beach ball.
Answer: A small iron ball can be heavier than a big beach ball

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a big balloon must be heavier than a small stone. Help Gappu understand.
teach.praise: The little stone is heavier! I must lift to compare, not just look at size.
teach.nudge: Does a bigger size always mean heavier? How can you check?

focus: Order things from heaviest to lightest
Know that size does not always decide weight
Find half of a weight in grams
remember: Half of 1 kg is 500 g
A small stone can be heavier than a big balloon
3 kg = 3000 g, so half is 1500 g = 1 kg 500 g
traps: The same size does not mean the same weight
Half of 1 kg is not 50 g or 200 g
Don't halve only the kilograms

topics.title: Estimating and using a pan balance

learn.hook: Is your water bottle less than 1 kg, about 1 kg or more than 1 kg? Guess, then check on a balance!
points: Estimate: hold a 1 kg packet in one hand and an object in the other. Is it lighter, about the same, or heavier?
A pan balance has two pans. The heavier side goes down; the lighter side goes up.
If both sides are level, the weights are equal.
Put a 1 kg weight on one side and the object on the other to check your estimate.
Predict the tilt: if one side has 2 kg and the other 1 kg 500 g, the 2 kg side goes down.

example.q: A pan balance has a pineapple on the left and a 1 kg weight on the right. The left pan goes down. What does this tell you?
steps: So the pineapple weighs more than 1 kg.
example.answer: The pineapple is more than 1 kg

learn.reallife: Old shops used pan balances with metal weights. Many sabziwalas still use them today.

games.title: Less than, about, or more than 1 kg?
Which way will it tilt?
items: 600 g on the left and 400 g on the right: the left goes down.
1 kg on the left and 1000 g on the right: the balance stays level.
The lighter side of a balance goes down.
750 g on the left and 1 kg on the right: the right goes down.
2 kg on the left and 1 kg 900 g on the right: it stays level.
2000 g is more than 1900 g, so the left goes down.

quiz.q: On a pan balance, which side goes down?
quiz.explain: The heavier side pulls its pan down.
steps: A pan balance is like a see-saw.
The heavier side pulls its pan down.
So the heavier side goes down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the lighter side goes down

quiz.q: A balance is level with a cabbage on one side and a 1 kg weight on the other. How heavy is the cabbage?
quiz.explain: Level means equal weights, so the cabbage weighs about 1 kg.
steps: The balance is level, so both sides weigh the same.
One side has a 1 kg weight.
So the cabbage weighs about 1 kg.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what level means

quiz.q: Which object is most likely less than 1 kg?
quiz.explain: A banana weighs only about 100 to 150 g.
steps: 1 kg is about a bag of sugar.
A jackfruit, a gas cylinder and a sack of rice are much heavier.
A ripe banana is only about 100 to 150 g, less than 1 kg.

quiz.q: Left pan: 800 g. Right pan: 1 kg. What happens?
quiz.explain: 1 kg = 1000 g is heavier than 800 g, so the right goes down.
steps: So the right pan (1 kg) goes down.
Answer: The right pan goes down

quiz.q: Left pan: 1 kg 200 g. Right pan: 1200 g. What happens?
quiz.explain: 1 kg 200 g = 1200 g. They are equal.
steps: Change to grams: 1 kg 200 g = 1000 + 200 = 1200 g.
Equal weights, so it stays level.

quiz.q: Rinku guessed his tiffin box weighs more than 1 kg. On the balance, the 1 kg side went down. Was he right?
options: No, the tiffin is less than 1 kg
quiz.explain: The 1 kg side went down, so it is heavier. The tiffin is less than 1 kg.
steps: On a balance, the heavier side goes down.
The 1 kg side went down, so 1 kg is heavier than the tiffin.
So No, the tiffin is less than 1 kg.
Answer: No, the tiffin is less than 1 kg
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which side is heavier

quiz.q: Left pan: 3 apples. Right pan: 1 small melon. The left pan goes up. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The side that goes up is lighter, so the melon is heavier.
steps: On a balance, the lighter side goes up.
The left pan (3 apples) went up, so it is lighter.

quiz.q: Left pan: 500 g + 250 g. Right pan: 700 g. Which way does it tilt?
quiz.explain: Left = 750 g, right = 700 g. Left is heavier, so it goes down.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the left side

teach.ask: Gappu put a mango on a pan balance with a 1 kg weight. The mango side went up. What does this tell Gappu?
teach.praise: The mango side went up, so it is lighter than 1 kg. Balances are fun!
teach.nudge: Which side goes down on a balance, and what does that mean?

revise.summary: A pan balance has two pans: the heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. If both sides are level, the weights are equal.
focus: Read what a pan balance shows
Predict which way a balance tilts
Check an estimate against a 1 kg weight
remember: Heavier side goes down; lighter side goes up
Level means the weights are equal
traps: The side that goes up is lighter, not heavier
Don't compare kg and g directly: 800 g is less than 1 kg (1000 g)
Don't compare one weight at a time; add up all the weights on each side first

learn.hook: Which is heavier: a kilo of cotton or a kilo of iron? Think before you answer!
points: We measure how heavy things are in grams (g) and kilograms (kg).
1 kilogram = 1000 grams.
Light things like a biscuit packet or a pencil are weighed in grams. Heavy things like a sack of rice or a person are weighed in kilograms.
1 kg of anything weighs the same as 1 kg of anything else.

example.q: A watermelon balances three 1 kg weights and one 500 g weight. How heavy is it in grams?

learn.reallife: At the sabzi mandi, the shopkeeper puts weights of 1 kg, 500 g and 250 g on the balance.

quiz.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
quiz.explain: 1 kilogram is the same as 1000 grams.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 kg is 100 g, like 1 m is 100 cm

quiz.q: How many grams are there in 3 kg?
Which unit is best for weighing a packet of biscuits?
quiz.explain: A biscuit packet is light, so grams are best. Litres are for liquids and metres are for length.
steps: Light things are weighed in grams.
Litre is for liquids and metre for length, so: Gram.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that measures something else

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 1 kg of cotton or 1 kg of iron?
quiz.explain: Both weigh exactly 1 kg. The cotton just takes up much more space.
steps: Cotton just takes up much more space than iron.
quiz.mistake: Thinks iron is always heavier because it feels hard

quiz.q: How many grams is 2 kg 500 g?
quiz.mistake: Writes 2 and 500 with a 0 in between

quiz.q: A bag of potatoes weighs 4000 g. How many kilograms is that?
Joseph puts weights of 500 g, 250 g and 250 g on a balance. What is the total weight?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the weights

quiz.q: A watermelon balances three 1 kg weights and one 500 g weight. How heavy is the watermelon?
quiz.mistake: Writes 3 and 5 together without thinking of place value

teach.ask: Gappu's bag says 1500 g and Kabir's says 1 kg 500 g. Whose bag is heavier?
teach.praise: Wow! 1 kg is 1000 g, so 1 kg 500 g is 1500 g. They weigh the same!
teach.nudge: How many grams are there in 1 kg? Try changing Kabir's weight to grams.

revise.summary: We measure how heavy things are in grams (g) and kilograms (kg); 1 kilogram = 1000 grams. Light things are weighed in grams and heavy things in kilograms.
focus: Change kg to g and g to kg
Choose g or kg for an object
Add weights on a balance
remember: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams
1 kg of anything weighs the same as 1 kg of anything else
traps: 1 kg is not 100 g
Don't divide or multiply by 100 instead of 1000
1 kg of iron is not heavier than 1 kg of cotton

learn.hook: Two 250 g packets balance one 500 g packet. Four of them make a whole kilogram!
points: Two 250 g packets = 500 g. Four 250 g packets = 1000 g = 1 kg.
Two 500 g packets also make 1 kg.
Use a known small weight to measure: if an eraser weighs 10 g, then 50 g balances 5 erasers.
To pack a weight, combine boxes: 1 kg = 500 g + 250 g + 250 g, or 500 g + 500 g, or ten 100 g boxes.

example.q: An eraser weighs 10 g. How many erasers balance a 50 g weight?

learn.reallife: Sweet shops pack 250 g, 500 g and 1 kg boxes. They can make any order by mixing box sizes.

quiz.q: How many 250 g packets balance one 500 g packet?
steps: One packet is 250 g; the other side is 500 g.

quiz.q: How many 250 g packets make 1 kg?
An eraser weighs 10 g. How many erasers weigh the same as 50 g?
A sharpener weighs 20 g. How many sharpeners balance 100 g?
Which boxes pack exactly 750 g?
steps: Only 500 g + 250 g packs exactly 750 g.

quiz.q: Which set does NOT make 1 kg?
steps: 3 × 250 = 750 g, so three 250 g boxes do NOT make 1 kg.

quiz.q: How many 100 g boxes are needed for 1 kg 500 g?
A pan has a 500 g weight. Raju puts 250 g packets on the other pan until it balances. How many does he put?
steps: One side has 500 g. Each packet is 250 g.

teach.ask: Gappu needs to pack 1 kg of laddoos using 250 g boxes. How many boxes? Explain.
teach.praise: 1000 g ÷ 250 g = 4 boxes! Laddoo delivery ready.
teach.nudge: How many grams are in 1 kg, and how many 250s fit?

revise.summary: Small packets can balance bigger weights: four 250 g packets or two 500 g packets make 1 kg. Use a known small weight to measure others.
focus: Find how many packets balance a weight
Use a known small weight to measure
Combine boxes to pack an exact weight
remember: Two 250 g = 500 g. Four 250 g = 1 kg
Two 500 g packets make 1 kg
1 kg = 500 g + 250 g + 250 g, or ten 100 g boxes
traps: 1 kg is not 500 g
Divide, don't subtract, to find how many
Don't forget the 500 g part in 1 kg 500 g

learn.hook: Mummy's shopping bag is getting heavy! Let's add, subtract and share weights and liquids.
points: To add or subtract, first write both amounts in the same unit, like grams or millilitres.
Add kg with kg and g with g. If the grams make 1000 or more, change 1000 g into 1 kg.
To share equally, divide.
To compare, change both to the same unit first.

example.q: Mummy buys 2 kg 500 g of potatoes and 1 kg 750 g of onions. What is the total weight?

learn.reallife: Cooks measure flour and milk for recipes, and shopkeepers add weights to make a bill.

quiz.q: Mummy buys 2 kg 500 g of potatoes and 1 kg 750 g of onions. What is the total weight?
quiz.mistake: Adds the grams but does not change 1000 g into 1 kg

quiz.q: A bag holds 5 kg of rice. 1200 g is used for a family function. How much rice is left?

quiz.mistake: Takes out the bucket only once

quiz.q: Each laddoo weighs 50 g. How many laddoos make 1 kg?

quiz.q: Harpreet's school bag weighs 3 kg. She adds a 750 g lunch box. What does the bag weigh now, in grams?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 + 750 without changing kg into g

teach.ask: Gappu added 2 kg and 300 g and got 302 g. What went wrong?
teach.praise: I see! First change 2 kg into 2000 g, then add 300 g. That makes 2300 g!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu add kilograms and grams directly? What should Gappu change first?

revise.summary: To add or subtract weights or capacities, first write both in the same unit. If the grams make 1000 or more, change 1000 g into 1 kg; to share equally, divide.
focus: Add and subtract weights in kg and g
Solve capacity problems in l and ml
Share equally and compare after changing units
remember: Add kg with kg and g with g
Change 1000 g into 1 kg
traps: Don't forget to change 1000 g into 1 kg
Don't subtract kg from g (or l from ml); change to the same unit first
Don't forget there are 2 bottles when comparing

learn.hook: The kirana shop, the doctor's clinic and the railway parcel office all have weighing machines. Are they the same?
points: A pan balance compares two sides using weights.
A kitchen scale weighs small amounts like flour or butter in grams.
A bathroom scale weighs people. A platform scale weighs heavy things like sacks and luggage.
A digital scale shows the weight as numbers on a screen, like 1.250 kg.
Things we lift easily usually weigh a few hundred grams to a few kg. Things we lift with effort weigh many kg.

example.q: Which machine should a railway parcel office use for a 60 kg trunk?
steps: A kitchen scale is for small amounts.
A platform scale weighs heavy things.

learn.reallife: At the doctor's, you stand on a scale to check your weight. At the airport, bags go on a big platform scale.

games.title: Sensible weights?
items: A school bag weighs about 4 g.
A Grade 4 child weighs about 30 kg.
A child's bicycle is about 10 to 15 kg.

quiz.q: Which machine is best to weigh a child at a clinic?
quiz.explain: A bathroom or person scale is made to weigh people.
steps: A child is heavy: many kilograms.
A bathroom (person) scale is made to weigh people.
A pan balance with 10 g weights or a kitchen scale is for small things.
quiz.mistake: Picks a scale for small amounts

quiz.q: Which is a sensible weight for an apple?

steps: An apple is small and fits in your hand.
quiz.mistake: Picks a weight that is far too big or small

quiz.q: Which can a Grade 4 child lift easily?

steps: A scooter, a fridge and a 50 kg sack are very heavy.
A 1 kg sugar packet is light.
So a child can easily lift the 1 kg sugar packet.

quiz.q: A shopkeeper weighs 250 g of cashews. Which machine is best?
quiz.explain: Small amounts are weighed on a kitchen or digital scale.

Small amounts are weighed on a kitchen or digital scale.
Platform scales and weighbridges are for heavy loads.
quiz.mistake: Picks a machine for heavy loads

quiz.q: Which is the most sensible weight for a Grade 4 child?
quiz.explain: Most Grade 4 children weigh between 20 and 40 kg.
steps: Most Grade 4 children weigh between 20 and 40 kg.
3 kg is a baby; 300 kg and 300 g are far off.
So about 30 kg is the most sensible.
quiz.mistake: Picks a weight far too small or big

quiz.q: Which is the best estimate for a full school bag?
quiz.explain: A bag with books weighs a few kilograms.
steps: A school bag full of books weighs a few kilograms.
4 g and 40 g are far too light; 400 kg is far too heavy.

quiz.q: Which needs effort to lift?

quiz.q: A digital scale shows 1.500 kg for a bag of onions. How many grams is that?

teach.praise: Kitchen scales are for small amounts. A platform scale is for heavy sacks!
teach.nudge: Which machine suits heavy things and which suits light things?

revise.summary: Different machines weigh different things: a kitchen scale for small amounts, a bathroom scale for people and a platform scale for heavy things. Choose sensible weights for real objects.
focus: Choose the right weighing machine
Pick sensible weights for objects and children
Read a digital scale
remember: Pan balance compares two sides; kitchen scale weighs small amounts in grams
Bathroom scale for people; platform scale for sacks and luggage

traps: Don't mix up g and kg

Big bags are often 10 kg, 20 kg, 25 kg or 50 kg.
Count how many 1 kg packets make a big bag: 10 kg = 10 packets of 1 kg.
25 kg = 25 packets of 1 kg. 50 kg = 50 packets.

learn.hook: How many glasses of nimbu paani can you pour from one big jug? Let's find out!
points: Capacity is how much liquid a container can hold.
We measure capacity in millilitres (ml) and litres (l).
1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
Small amounts like a spoon of medicine are in ml. Big amounts like a bucket of water are in litres.
2 l 250 ml means 2000 ml + 250 ml = 2250 ml.

topics.title: Market survey: by weight or by volume?

points: Solids like rice, dal, sugar, vegetables and fruit are sold by weight (g or kg).

topics.title: How much water do we use?

learn.hook: Drip, drip, drip... A leaking tap can waste a whole bucket of water every day!
points: Put a mug under a leaking tap for one hour and measure the water collected.
Daily loss = loss in 1 hour × 24 hours. Weekly loss = daily loss × 7.
If a tap leaks 500 ml in an hour, it wastes 24 × 500 = 12,000 ml = 12 L a day, and 84 L a week.
Ways to save water: fix leaks, close the tap while brushing, use a bucket not a shower, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants.
